mcp.title: Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server
mcp.blurb: Connect autonomous AI agents (Antigravity, Claude Desktop, Cursor, VS Code with Roo Code/Cline, or local models via Ollama/LM Studio) directly to PZ Mod Studio. The MCP server gives them the console log, crash reports, the files two mods both replace, a Lua syntax check and control of the running game.
mcp.generatorBlurb: Select your AI client or environment and copy the JSON snippet into your configuration file:
mcp.important: Important: Do NOT run pz-mcp-server.exe directly by double-clicking
mcp.importantBlurb: If you double-click pz-mcp-server.exe, a black command prompt will open and stay blank. This is completely normal. The MCP server communicates silently over stdio (JSON-RPC) with AI agents. You do not need to keep it open; your AI assistant (Claude, Cursor, Antigravity) will launch and close it automatically in the background whenever you send prompts in chat.

claude.title: How to set it up in Claude Desktop:
claude.s1: Open Claude Desktop and go to File > Settings (or press Ctrl + ,).
claude.s2: Select the Developer tab and click Edit Config to open claude_desktop_config.json.
claude.s3: Paste the JSON configuration above inside the file and save it.
claude.s4: Restart Claude Desktop. In new chats you will see a 🔨 Hammer icon with the PZ Mod Studio tools.
claude.tip: 💬 Example prompt: "Read console.txt to diagnose why Project Zomboid crashed" or "Sort my mod load order".

cursor.title: How to set it up in Cursor / Windsurf:
cursor.s4: The status dot turns green (Enabled) and the agent can use the Studio's tools.
cursor.tip: 💬 Example prompt: "@pz-mod-studio find the files my active mods both replace and merge the scripts".

vscode.title: How to set it up in VS Code (Roo Code / Cline, with local or cloud models):
vscode.s1: Install the Roo Code or Cline extension from the VS Code Marketplace.
vscode.s2: Click the extension's icon in the sidebar, open the MCP Servers tab at the top and choose Configure MCP.
vscode.s4: Cloud models work, and so do local ones with Ollama / LM Studio (e.g. Qwen 2.5 Coder).
vscode.tip: 🔒 Offline: with a local model, the Studio's tools (file conflicts, Lua checks, logs) work without an internet connection.

antigravity.title: How to set it up in Antigravity / Gemini CLI:
antigravity.s1: Open your Antigravity or Gemini CLI settings file (.gemini/settings.json or the user settings).
antigravity.s2: Paste the snippet under the "mcpServers" section.
antigravity.s3: Antigravity finds and connects every tool and resource on its own.
antigravity.tip: 💬 Example prompt: "Read console.txt and tell me which mod is failing and how to fix it".

openai.title: How to set it up in OpenAI / Codex / other MCP bridges:
openai.s1: Point your MCP client or local stdio bridge at the executable as its command.
openai.s2: The server describes its tools following the JSON-RPC 2.0 MCP standard (2024-11-05).
openai.s3: Make sure the process is started with standard input and output pipes (stdio).

bisect.intro: For what the log cannot tell you: a freeze, a recipe that never appears, a save that will not open. Half your mods go off, you play, and the half that still does it is halved again. About 8 launches find one mod among a hundred.

The game skips the item and carries on; that item is gone from the save.

translator_text.explanation: A text in a mod's translation file (a sandbox option's name or tooltip, usually) has a % that is not written %%, so Java's text formatting cannot read it. The game shows the text as it is and carries on: nothing else breaks.
translator_text.action: Nothing to do to play. The fix is in the mod's translation file (% written as %%); "Save report" names the mod, the file and the line.

nil_table.explanation: Mod code attempted to access properties of a nil/uninitialized table before PZ Build 42 instantiated it.

java_npe.title: Java Interop Null Pointer Exception

kahlua.title: Lua Runtime Execution Crash (Kahlua)

kahlua.action: Apply Universal Master Polyfills to protect game loops and callframe stacktraces.

index_bounds.title: Multiplayer Java ArrayList Out of Bounds (B42)
index_bounds.explanation: A mod accessed IsoPlayer.getPlayers() or getOnlinePlayers() index 0 while the Java player collection was empty during a render/tick loop in Multiplayer.
index_bounds.action: Apply Universal Master Polyfills (Safe ArrayList Proxy & getOnlinePlayers shield).

fancy_handwork.title: Fancy Handwork Multiplayer Hand Sync Safety
fancy_handwork.explanation: Fancy Handwork fancyMP loop threw an uncaught error when evaluating local/remote player hand objects on tick.
fancy_handwork.action: Apply Universal Master Polyfills to guard FancyHandwork callbacks safely.

sauced_carts.title: SaucedCarts Pushable Carts Multiplayer Sync

saves.title: Saves
saves.blurb: PZ Mod Studio backs a save up when you leave it, before it loads with mods that changed since its last session, and before its mod list is changed. Each backup is a zip read back after it is written. The newest {{keep}} automatic backups of each save are kept; the ones you make or pin stay until you remove them.

saves.empty: No saves yet. Start a game and it shows here.
saves.noRoom: Not enough free space for a backup of {{size}}.
saves.noBackups: No backups of this save yet.

saves.unkeepTitle: Stop keeping it: it becomes an automatic backup again

saves.deleteConfirm: Remove the backup of {{when}} of "{{world}}"? This cannot be undone.
saves.unchangedKept: "{{world}}" has not changed since its last backup, which is now kept.
saves.restored: "{{world}}" is back as it was on {{when}}. The save as it was is in its backups.
saves.unkept: The backup of {{when}} is an automatic one again.

whatsNew.blurb: Your Workshop mods updated since you last played, and the ones whose update is waiting in Steam, with each update's change notes. "May break saves" is a guess (a map mod, or notes that talk about new saves, wipes, things removed or renamed): read the notes before you load a save in progress. An update still waiting in Steam can be headed off by keeping the version you have first.

maps.title: Maps
maps.blurb: Every cell of the world, over the game's own map: the game's world (grey outline) and each installed map mod's cells. A map mod's cells over the game's world replace what was there. Two map mods with cells in common fight over them (red): what one built there is gone, unless one builds on the other (its map.info names it in lots=). One cell is 256 x 256 tiles.
maps.onlyActive: Only map mods on in my list
maps.clashNow: {{a}} and {{b}} share {{count}} cell(s) and both are on: in the next game one replaces the other there.
maps.clashIf: {{a}} and {{b}} share {{count}} cell(s): they would clash if both were on.
maps.none: No installed mod adds cells to the world.
maps.relatedBlurb: These mods are about maps but add no cells of their own: spawn points or a map list for another map, or the tiles and textures maps are built from. They need what they are for to be on (the map, or the mod that uses the tiles).
maps.tiledefNow: Tile definition number {{number}} is used by {{mods}}, and more than one is on: their tiles overwrite each other (wrong walls, floors or furniture). Keep only one of them on.
maps.tiledefIf: Tile definition number {{number}} is used by {{mods}}: only one of them can be on at a time.

join.searchBlurb: Asks Steam for every Project Zomboid server, the way the game's own browser does, through the Steam client already running on this PC (no key needed; Steam shows you as in Project Zomboid while it asks). Servers appear as they answer; it takes about a minute and a half for all of them.

join.addBlurb: For a private server or a friend's: the address they gave you. The password is kept in Windows' credential store, never in a file.

join.partialBlurb: A server only announces the first few of its mods (Steam cuts the list at 127 characters). The full list is known once you join it from here.
join.notInstalled: Not installed: the game downloads it when you join
join.joinBlurb: Starts the game on this server's connect window (close the game first), with the server password and your username filled in. There you type your account password and press Connect; the button stays off without a username. A new username makes a new account on that server. The game downloads the server's mods and uses them only there: your own mod list and profiles stay as they are.
